summary: No reviewed primary source validates three Korean long-only recommendations all gaining at least 10% inside five sessions without loss. Evidence supports testable hypotheses and cost/microstructure constraints, with important Korean nonreplications.

rows.title: Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency
rows.costs: Abstract reports bid-ask and plausible-cost corrections
rows.finding: Weekly winners and losers reverse the following week; interpreted as liquidity-market inefficiency.
rows.applicability: Weekly horizon relevant; broad long-short portfolio, not three Korean long-only names or a 10% target.
rows.quality: Original QJE publisher abstract; full empirical tables not accessed

rows.title: Evaporating Liquidity
rows.holding: Daily return-reversal portfolios using lags 1–5 days
rows.costs: Highlighted 1998–2010 strategy examples are before execution costs
rows.finding: Liquidity-provision returns vary strongly with VIX; high expected returns in market stress reflect constrained liquidity supply.
rows.applicability: A rising expected rebound payoff is not a no-loss guarantee; diversified market-hedged long-short result cannot justify selecting distressed high-ATR longs.
rows.quality: Original author NBER working paper with methodological detail

rows.title: Another look at trading costs and short-term reversal profits
rows.costs: Keim–Madhavan model and Nomura trading cost estimates; US up to 30–50bp/week net, Europe up to 20bp/week under liquid-universe/low-turnover design
rows.finding: Avoiding costly small caps and reducing turnover materially changes whether reversal survives costs.
rows.applicability: Strong support for liquidity/cost constraints; payoff scale and diversification are far from three stocks each +10%.
rows.quality: Original accepted paper in university repository; authors include Robeco practitioners

rows.title: Short-term Momentum
rows.holding: Previous-month return × share turnover; monthly short-term momentum
rows.costs: Author abstract reports survival after transaction costs
rows.finding: High-turnover stocks show continuation, low-turnover stocks reversal; continuation strongest in large liquid covered stocks.
rows.applicability: Turnover is not today's volume/20-day-average-volume; monthly findings do not validate 5-day Korean breakouts.
rows.quality: Original authors' SSRN accepted-version abstract; details not fully read

rows.title: 한국주식시장의 단기반전과 단기모멘텀
rows.costs: Controls size/microstructure/arbitrage constraints/T+2; net-cost implementation not established by accessible abstract
rows.finding: No high-turnover short-term momentum replication; reversal persists across turnover groups and is stronger in small illiquid stocks.
rows.applicability: Direct negative transfer evidence against importing US high-turnover momentum wholesale; different horizon from 1–5 days.
rows.quality: KCI official journal record with original Korean/English abstract; DOI 10.22510/kjofm.2023.40.4.008

rows.title: 비유동성 및 거래비용과 단기반전현상을 이용한 반대투자전략의 성과에 관한 연구
rows.holding: Short-term contrarian strategies; exact rebalance interval not verified from abstract
rows.costs: Effective-spread transaction costs eliminate abnormal profits
rows.finding: Reversal is stronger with high turnover/illiquidity, but observed gross alpha vanishes after measured costs.
rows.applicability: Do not select illiquid crash rebounds because historical gross bounce looks large; old market period is a limitation.
rows.quality: Original publisher Seoul National University repository and original abstract

rows.title: Decomposing Short-Term Return Reversal
rows.costs: Spread-based estimate about 80.5bp/month vs three-factor alpha 1.34%/month
rows.finding: Reversal profits concentrate in residual nonfundamental price moves, not cash-flow news; industry and earnings-news decomposition matters.
rows.applicability: Supports separating liquidity shock from fundamental bad news; raw decline/high ATR is insufficient. Needs sector and point-in-time earnings/analyst data.
rows.quality: Original NY Fed research staff paper; estimates are historical, not modern Korean execution costs

rows.title: A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns
rows.costs: Paper explicitly notes transaction costs reduce strategy attractiveness; not a net-cost 5-day stock-picking test
rows.finding: Return continuation within overnight or intraday components coexists with reversal across them. Momentum/reversal premia accrue overnight in the studied strategies.
rows.applicability: Forecast/measure recommendation-open-to-close separately from prior-close-to-open; daily close-to-close momentum cannot promise same-day green candles.
rows.quality: Original accepted refereed paper in LSE repository

rows.title: The short-term mean reversion of stock price and the change in trading volume
rows.holding: Variance-ratio tests from 1 to 100 days, five-day base interval
rows.costs: No executable net-cost trading strategy established
rows.finding: Significant contemporaneous return/volume-change stocks exhibit sub-five-day continuation and longer reversal; post-2000 KOSDAQ sub-five-day continuation differs from KOSPI.
rows.applicability: A plausible OHLCV-only interaction hypothesis; statistical variance dynamics do not prove a 10% target hit strategy. Note source's sample-period inconsistency.
rows.quality: Original open-access article PDF mirror, DOI 10.1108/JDQS-01-2021-0003; full result paragraphs read

rows.title: Individual Investors and Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Evidence from Korea
rows.market: Korean equities with daily investor-type trading
rows.costs: Reported abnormal returns; net transaction-cost result not verified
rows.finding: Positive earnings-surprise quintile drift reaches 3.51% at 60 days; negative-surprise quintile −1.63% at 20 days. Drift linked to individual contrarian trading, foreigners anticipate/exploit surprises.
rows.applicability: Useful event-quality direction; holding period/average payoff do not justify five-day +10%. Requires timestamped earnings surprise and investor flow data.
rows.quality: Original author paper hosted by finance journal; exact publication year unresolved

rows.title: Stock Price Reactions to News and the Momentum Effect in the Korean Stock Market
rows.holding: News/momentum portfolios; exact interval not verified from publisher abstract
rows.costs: Authors associate asymmetric reactions with transaction costs; net executable strategy not verified
rows.finding: News losers show continued negative drift; winner reversals offset those momentum profits. Overall momentum strategy earns no profits in the studied sample.
rows.applicability: Strong reason not to treat any crash as a benign oversold rebound; news/catalyst sign matters. Does not establish long-only news-winner spikes.
rows.quality: Original Wiley journal abstract, Lee and Cho, APJFS43:556–588

rows.title: Trading Behavior, Performance, and Stock Preference of Foreigners, Local Institutions, and Individual Investors
rows.holding: Short-term performance; exact horizon not verified from accessible abstract
rows.costs: Net-cost result not established by accessible abstract
rows.finding: Foreigners' purchases outperform sales; foreigners prefer larger high-dividend stocks while individual investors prefer small high-leverage low-dividend stocks.
rows.applicability: Investor-flow data can be a separate candidate confirmation; cannot infer daily +10% success from aggregate investor outperformance.
rows.quality: KCI official record with original authors' abstract; DOI 10.1111/j.2041-6156.2011.01037.x

rows.title: Dynamic and Static Volatility Interruptions: Evidence from the Korean Stock Markets
rows.holding: Intraday microstructure around VI introduction, 45 days before/after
rows.costs: Market-quality study, not net trading P&L strategy
rows.finding: VI events concentrate in small, low-priced, volatile names; dynamic VI contributes more to stabilization/discovery than static VI.
rows.applicability: High volatility and price-limit proximity have execution and stability implications, not inherently favorable expected return.
rows.quality: Original peer-reviewed paper using KRX-provided intraday data

rows.title: Guide to Trading in the Korean Stock Market
rows.finding: Daily ±30% limits; opening/closing call auctions; VI switches to two-minute call auction and triggering quote is not executed at potential execution price.
rows.applicability: Daily high touching target is not proof that any quantity could exit there; use conservative fill and gap assumptions.
rows.quality: Official exchange guide; corroborated VI with current KRX regulation page

rows.title: 종목별 변동성완화장치 and 단기과열완화제도
rows.holding: VI two-minute call; overheating designation three days of 30-minute calls
rows.costs: No continuous-execution assumption during designated periods
rows.finding: Overheating designation changes regular continuous matching to 30-minute call auctions for three sessions; designation can extend.
rows.applicability: Exclude or explicitly model designated/limited/halted names. OHLCV cannot recover executable stop/target sequence.
rows.quality: Current official KRX regulations, including 2025 NXT-related turnover treatment update

rows.title: 한국투자증권 최선집행기준 설명서
rows.holding: Intraday; NXT 08:00 premarket and after-hours differ from KRX
rows.costs: Distinguishes explicit commissions/fees from implicit market impact; execution also considers fill likelihood
rows.finding: Orders may route differently by session and venue; resting limit-order fills and automatic transfer are not guaranteed.
rows.applicability: Choose consistent KRX versus combined market data/entry definition; morning recommendation benchmark must match a tradable venue and time.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Liquidity-aware short-term reversal as a comparator only
hypotheses.data: OHLCV: turnover value and Amihud-style impact proxy; shares outstanding needed for true share turnover
hypotheses.reason: Reversal profits are sensitive to expensive small caps and costs; distress alone is not a catalyst

hypotheses.hypothesis: Separate overnight gap and intraday return continuation
hypotheses.data: Existing split-adjusted OHLCV, strictly prior to signal cutoff
hypotheses.reason: Close-to-close momentum can combine opposite-sign overnight and intraday effects; evaluate same-day candle and five-day exit separately

hypotheses.hypothesis: Volume-change interaction with trend/return rather than unconditional high-volume bonus
hypotheses.data: Existing historical OHLCV permits lagged rolling return/volume-change correlation; fit only prior windows
hypotheses.reason: Korean sub-five-day evidence is statistical and conditional; recent high-volume levels alone do not imply continuation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Positive earnings/news with investor-flow confirmation; negative-event crash exclusion
hypotheses.data: New timestamped DART earnings surprises, news/event classifications, daily foreign/institutional/individual net buying, PIT availability
hypotheses.reason: Korean PEAD/news evidence distinguishes good and bad information; do not infer event quality from large ATR or oversold RSI

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tradeability-aware eligibility and conservative target/stop simulation
hypotheses.data: New PIT trading-status/overheating/halts and limit state; tick or intraday bars if target-stop order matters; explicit slippage/fees/tax assumptions
hypotheses.reason: KRX auctions and liquidity can invalidate OHLC touch fills and guaranteed loss caps

implementation_limits: Keep UI and copy frozen. Apply original technical-score threshold as eligibility, never inflate/remap numeric scores.
Literature does not identify a validated exact technical-score cutoff or ATR cutoff for this product. Quantitative thresholds require chronological out-of-sample evaluation.
For daily OHLC, if both stop and target are touched and ordering is unknown, use a conservative ordering assumption and report ambiguity rather than assuming the target came first.

Backtest from recommendation-time executable entry (e.g. next KRX open with slippage), include gaps, suspensions/unfilled buys, costs and five-session final exit, alongside target-hit and adverse-excursion statistics.
Do not describe abstract-only findings as a replicated strategy; do not confuse long-short factor average returns with three individual long-only stock outcomes.
